name: shadow-text

frames.best_why: Long shadows stretch left from every letter while the full headline, subtitle and button stay visible.

tagline: Big headline letters cast long shadows that swing away from the pointer.
summary: A hero heading whose letters throw long, soft shadows angled by the time of day or by the pointer acting as a lamp. A subtitle and call-to-action button sit beneath.
appearance: A large white sans-serif headline sits centred in a dark rounded panel above a muted subtitle and a small white pill button. Each letter carries a long soft black shadow stretching away, and a tiny mono line at the bottom-left records the time.
behaviour: The shadows rest at an angle set from the clock and tick forward every half minute. Moving the pointer near the text turns it into a lamp, so every letter's shadow swings and stretches away from the cursor.
demo_content: Headline 'Golden hour, every day.', a Lumen photo-time subtitle, a Get Lumen button and a 'Shadows set for' note.
search_phrases: text that casts a shadow from the cursor
use_when: A landing hero needs a large headline that reacts to the pointer without images or extra weight.
avoid_when: Long shadows only read on a plain contrasting surface; on busy backgrounds they dissolve into noise.
customise: The headline is passed as children; the element tag, clock-driven lighting, pointer takeover and shadow reach are props, while the shadow formula is fixed.
weight_why: A few dozen letter spans and a short rAF that runs only while the shadows settle.

a11y.note: The visual letters are hidden from assistive tech with a plain copy provided; reduced motion snaps shadows instead of animating.

polish_why: Long shadows read cleanly and the pointer lamp feels physical; the surrounding copy is plain.
